newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN'S TABAREZ TOLD HE STILL HAS A JOB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN'S TABAREZ TOLD HE STILL HAS A JOB.

text.p: AC Milan's owner Silvio Berlusconi has told manager Oscar Washington Tabarez his job is safe despite the 2-1 defeat by IFK Gothenburg in the European Champions' League, Italian newspapers reported on Thursday.

They said the media mogul and former prime minister had called his Uruguayan coach on Wednesday night after the Italian champions succumbed to the Swedish part-timers in their fifth defeat of the season.
"You have my full confidence," Berlusconi told Tabarez, according to the reports.

A source close to the billionaire politician was unable to confirm the conversation but said Berlusconi had watched the game from the Rome headquarters of his Forza Italia party and put the defeat down to "typical bad luck".
The source said Berlusconi had telephoned managing director Adriano Galliani in Gothenburg and asked him to "tell the boys that I'm happy with them and the way they fought".
"In that sense, he reassured Tabarez," the source said.
Tabarez was brought in on a one-year contract when coach Fabio Capello left for Real Madrid following five seasons of successes that included four serie A titles and a European Cup.
The defending champions now lie sixth in the league after crashing 3-0 to Roma last Saturday.
That disappointment fuelled speculation that Milan may dump Tabarez and try to lure back Capello's predecessor Arrigo Sacchi, whose job as Italy's national coach is now on the line.
Galliani dismissed such talk as nonsense in Gothenburg on Wednesday before the Champions' League clash.
"Releasing a coach from his contract is not part of our rules of behaviour," Galliani said.

"Therefore it's a big mistake to talk about releasing Tabarez. I've read reports that we've been in touch with Sacchi. We've got nothing of the sort in mind and the future will prove it," he told Italian reporters.

Milan took a 52nd minute lead in Gothenburg through Liberian striker George Weah but suddenly found themselves facing the real possiblity of being knocked out of Europe after the Swedes scored twice in 10 minutes.

With Milan unsettled by the loss of man of the match Tomas Locatelli to injury, substitute Erik Wahlstedt headed in Gothenburg's first in the 74th minute with the second in the 84th coming from Niclas Alexandersson.
The defeat left Milan second in Group D with three points after just one win from three matches and with a huge incentive for revenge when they face Gothenburg at home on October 30.
Unbeaten Porto head the group on nine points.
Tabarez, whose team had contested Gothenburg's winning goal as offside, said Milan had not deserved to lose.

"You can't train for luck but I really have to say that fortune didn't knock at our door," he said. "They managed to turn round the game in the last 15 minutes but had absolutely not deserved to win."
